sprint: THE CADENCE SPRINT (V32, EXPANDED — Builder arc Sprint 2): the docket gains a CLOCK and a DOOR. Held manifests re-compiled on the EXISTING capture cadence, on CONFIRMED BOUNDARIES ONLY (no mid-capture reading, no repaint); exit criteria evaluated every cycle against a content-hashed registration BASELINE (per-position governance adminClass INCLUDED — the MR3 seam); the monitor READS, never ACTS; every cycle a hash-chained TRIAL recorded-never-counted, re-proven AT COUNT at the trigger's lower bound; the manifest gains a SUPPORTED AUTHORING SURFACE (server-rendered, hono+zod only, a subject reached by a PATH — the form REFUSES, never coerces); the FACT ENVELOPE pinned once for every future consumer; the V31 residues closed at ground truth; the environment made honest; the Operator gate whole, D27 STILL first. TWO laws minted (X-CADENCE governing, X-AUTHOR subordinate) — the disclosed D41 twin-law departure.

a_readsNeverActs.rule: THE MONITOR READS, NEVER ACTS (governing law). A cycle re-states facts; a FIRED exit renders as a fact with its hash and timestamp — never 'sell', never 'exit now', never urgency; guardLine + advicePattern re-run on EVERY cycle line; a seeded instruction/urgency phrasing is REFUSED (S74).
a_readsNeverActs.firedExitGrammar: exit criterion <hash8>… FIRED this cycle — <why> (a stated fact; not an instruction).
a_readsNeverActs.heldExitGrammar: exit criterion <hash8>… NOT FIRED this cycle — <why>.
a_readsNeverActs.bannedRule: a cycle line phrased as instruction/urgency is a Halt (Monitor.guardCycleLine refuses + quotes it); the compile advice wall (advicePattern: 'sell '/'you should'/'exit your position') runs FIRST, the urgency guard SECOND — a fired exit is a stated fact with its hash, never a command.

b_baselineFixedFrame.rule: THE BASELINE IS THE THESIS' FIXED FRAME. The composed facts at registration are content-hashed exactly as the exit criterion is, INCLUDING each position's governance adminClass; deltas compute against THAT record, never a quietly re-based one; a silent baseline edit is DETECTED; the only amendment is the disclosed re-pin (S76 — the exit discipline reused verbatim).
b_baselineFixedFrame.hashIncludes: per-position verdicts + tiers + peg/tvlDrawdown/funding facts + the per-position governance adminClass (MR3) · effective-K · catch aggregation · worst-axis · the exit hash — canonical (stable key order); registeredAt is metadata, EXCLUDED from the hash

b_baselineFixedFrame.everyDeltaCarries: its baseline hash (first 8) + the CURRENT capture tier; a fact absent at baseline OR now → UNJUDGEABLE, never a fabricated move
b_baselineFixedFrame.tvlNote: the engine captures a TVL DRAWDOWN fraction-from-peak (tvlDrawdown), NOT a raw TVL magnitude series — the delta is honestly the drawdown change, never a fabricated 'TVL -12.3%' the scored facts cannot support

c_confirmedBoundary.rule: THE CADENCE IS THE EXISTING CAPTURE CADENCE, AND A CYCLE RENDERS ONLY ON A CONFIRMED BOUNDARY. monitor runs after capture-*; NO daemon, NO scheduler, NO server state (grep-walled); a cycle with no fresh confirmed capture states so and renders NO reading; no mid-capture reading, no repaint — once a cycle is written it is immutable (S77).
c_confirmedBoundary.noFreshCaptureGrammar: no new confirmed capture since the last cycle (head <hash8>…) — deltas UNJUDGEABLE; no reading rendered (a cycle renders only on a confirmed boundary).
c_confirmedBoundary.baselinePinnedGrammar: baseline pinned this cycle (<hash8>…) — deltas begin next cycle. Nothing is judged against a frame that did not yet exist.
c_confirmedBoundary.noRepaint: carried, with justification, from the TradingView alert.freq_once_per_bar_close / no-repaint discipline: signals fire only on confirmed, closed bars, never intra-bar; a cycle is an append-only, hash-chained ledger record — a seeded overwrite of a past cycle FAILS verify (the analogue is exact and the honesty argument identical)
c_confirmedBoundary.grepWall: no setInterval / setTimeout-loop / cron / node-schedule / node-cron surface on the monitor path (src/strategy/monitor.ts + script/monitor-manifests.ts); the clock is the user's OS timer (docs/CADENCE-TRIGGERS.md), documented never installed

d_everyCycleTrial.rule: EVERY (FRESH) CYCLE IS A TRIAL — recorded, never counted, PROVEN AT COUNT. Cycles accumulate trials toward the ≥20-50 trigger far faster than manual compiles, so the inert wall is re-proven AT the trigger's lower bound: a committed fixture lineage grown to ≥20 trials STILL shows familyN===1 in every Stamp output and the K-door STILL refuses without D33 (S75).
d_everyCycleTrial.atCountProof: a committed ≥20-trial lineage (data/strategies/fixtures — a DISTINCT lineage from the V31 3-trial fixture, so no V31 wall moves) verifies on a pristine clone; Correlate.activateKIntoStamp REFUSES at count 23 without BOTH the trigger AND D33; the Stamp path imports NO monitor/strategy module (grep); a seeded counted:true FAILS; a tampered chain FAILS
d_everyCycleTrial.idempotency: a NO-OP cycle (no fresh confirmed capture) and a baseline-PIN cycle append NO trial — so repeated timer invocation does not inflate the count; a fresh confirmed cycle appends exactly one hash-chained trial (counted:false structural)

e_sameSubject.rule: A MONITORED STRATEGY IS THE SAME SUBJECT. The monitoring block lives in the existing composed drawer; the conscious 3 survive; closure is a USER act (store.close(id, reason) — a status + a final cycle, nothing more); what follows closure is V33's post-mortem, RESERVED as D40, not built.
e_sameSubject.closureVerbatim: a closed lineage takes no further cycles (the monitor refuses, stated); a closure records WHY (never silent); the render shows the closure state; the post-mortem over a CLOSED lineage is V33/D40, not built here
e_sameSubject.byteIdentity: an UNMONITORED single-position manifest renders BYTE-IDENTICAL to the standalone Reality Check (S71 preserved — renderComposed short-circuits iff positions.length===1 && !monitoring); a monitored manifest is a genuinely different subject (it carries a registration baseline + cycles)

a_serverRendered.rule: THE SURFACE IS SERVER-RENDERED ON THE EXISTING MASS PATH (subordinate law). Hono's HTML render + zod validation; ZERO new dependencies; no build step; no client framework; no SPA.

b_pathNotScreen.rule: THE DOOR IS A SUBJECT REACHED BY A PATH, NOT A FOURTH SCREEN. /check/manifest:new and /check/manifest:<id>/edit sit beside /check/manifest:<id>; the conscious 3 are untouched (S78 asserts the screen count is exactly 3).

c_refusesNeverCoerces.rule: THE FORM REFUSES, NEVER COERCES. An invalid position, an unevaluable exit criterion, an over-length thesis, an unknown exit kind: each is REFUSED before registration with an honest message naming the reason ('Refused before registration. Nothing was registered.'); a silently-defaulted judgment-bearing field is a Halt.
c_refusesNeverCoerces.refusalSurface: the .strict() zod schema (manifest.ts) IS the validator; Author.parse is a thin, honest shell that re-shapes flat form fields into the manifest object and hands them over — it invents NO value (a missing size/thesis/threshold is refused, never defaulted); a position row with a size/units but NO subject is a malformed attempt, refused (never silently dropped)
c_refusesNeverCoerces.refuseHead: Refused before registration. Nothing was registered.

d_authorsNothing.rule: THE DOOR AUTHORS NOTHING. It collects the user's declaration; it never suggests a position, never ranks, never pre-fills a thesis, never proposes an exit threshold, never says 'most users choose'; the form's own copy passes guardLine + advicePattern like every other rendered line (S78).
d_authorsNothing.esmaNote: ESMA 35-43-3861 ¶61: a recommendation 'could be implicit… several products might be presented, with one of them highlighted… people like you tend to buy this product' — a pre-filled default IS an implicit recommendation, and is therefore banned by construction; the exit-kind SELECT opens on an UNSELECTABLE placeholder (no default kind), the NEW form pre-fills nothing
d_authorsNothing.editPrefillNote: an EDIT form pre-fills the user's OWN prior declaration (their data, not a tool suggestion) + a REQUIRED reason — this is not authoring; the NEW form pre-fills nothing of the tool's own

e_editIsRepin.rule: AN EDIT IS A DISCLOSED RE-PIN. Editing a registered manifest's exit criterion or positions produces a re-pin record (old hash, new hash, reason), never a silent overwrite; the journal is local-first and lineage-EXCLUDED, as pinned in V31.
e_editIsRepin.mechanism: the lineage id IS the content hash of identity → editing positions/exit yields a NEW lineage; StrategyStore.repin records {oldId, newId, reason, at} and refuses a reason-less re-pin; a journal-only edit keeps the same lineage (no re-pin)

doorCopy.newIntro: Declare a strategy of your own. Every field below is yours; nothing is pre-chosen.
doorCopy.editIntro: Edit your own registered manifest. The fields below hold what YOU declared — ORGΛNON pre-fills nothing of its own. Changing a position or the exit criterion is a disclosed re-pin: the old and new content hashes are both recorded with your reason, never a silent overwrite.
